{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "She did not step back from the ring. She had thought she would, when she understood, but her feet stayed where the salt had dried them to the boards, and the chart in her hands felt heavier than paper had any right to feel.

"Who tied you?" she asked.

He took his hand from the iron at last and looked at the palm, at the pale mark the cold had left there. "A woman with a chart," he said. "Different coast. Same circle."

"And before her?"

"There is always a before." He said it without weight, the way one might say the tide comes twice. "The sea on this side needs a shore to lean against, or it forgets it is a sea. It goes flat. It goes dark. You saw what it was like, crossing."

She had. The causeway had been dry, and the dry had gone on past the edges of her lantern in every direction, and she had told herself it was fog.

"How long," she said.

"Until someone draws the line past you." He nodded at the chart. "You did it yourself, at the reef. You were wrong, and you fixed it, and the fixing is what carried you here. Most people never fix it. They leave the mistake and sail around."

She folded the paper along its old creases. The circle vanished into the fold, and the two coastlines lay face to face in the dark.

"Sit down," she said. "You've been standing a long time."

He looked at her, and for the first time something in his face was not patience.

"Sit down," she said again, and knelt, and put both hands on the iron."}
